column8: Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3d guard: art. 3 makes a seal equal to a signature where a law requires writing, never more, so the report's seal stays a craft image; Taiwan law out of scope (case A13).

Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3c-3e context: a seal proves who signed (art. 358 presumption), not that money exists; row 39 says the same in craft terms without Taiwan law, so use that one; the 104台上2183 ruling stays UNVERIFIED.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; its guard serves the 3d writers: the registered identity seal (印鑑) and the calligrapher's art seal of Q47 A15 are different objects, never blurred in one sentence.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, registry colour; the dated-key mapping does no investing job a part needs.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the source of claim 1's correction (a registered seal proves identity to a land office in place of turning up); land rules, not pledges.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; a land-office rule for legal persons, seals filed beside internal approvals; a cash grant passes through no registry, so no part uses it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3d colour at most; registry practice, and the big and small seals would add a second seal image the one-turn rule cannot carry.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; one land office's fraud warning; the register-protects-the-owner mapping is a stretch and no part needs it.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, backs the 3d guard that a seal is an identity check, not what binds a company, and that even the registry is dropping company seals (MOEA letters of 2008 and 2026).

Mon 16 Nov: background to row 11; fix the dates: the Civil Code of 1929 applied in Taiwan only from 1945, so never from 1929 to 1999 in Taiwan or seventy years in Taiwan; the 1929 legislative reason re-read at source today (俾得確定法律之關係, exact).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d candidate turn beside the seal; the 1999 reason re-read at source today (一時情感因素, 經過公證之贈與, exact); fix the mapping: ink stays owned (the right moved, row 12), never a notary's deed or a moral duty, which is the signed sense card Q42 warns of; say in the same sentence that Laura's figure is ink because the Treasuries are held for her (row 37); context, never advice (case A13); the 1929 rule ran in Taiwan from 1945 (row 10).

Mon 16 Nov: store only, the truest legal echo of ink as owned: since 1999 a gift binds once the right has moved (權利移轉, re-read at source today), not when written or handed over; pairs with Q79-004 at 2.0; Taiwan law out of scope.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the 公證 and 認證 difference explains rows 14-15; never as advice on how a residency should read a co-sponsor's notarised letter (case A13).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; 52 of 61 notaries leaving the question to a court is vivid but legal detail; the Judicial Yuan text was read in a third-party copy, so S 4.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; fix the mapping only the deed is ink: ink never maps to a legal deed (card Q42, Q79-004); say a stamped signature does not make a promise to give binding; forum resolutions guide lower courts, not bind them; read in a copy.

Mon 16 Nov: re-read at source today: art. 82 says 以墨線填充或以其他方法表示其為空白, so a blank takes an ink line or another mark, never ink alone; as a 2.0 turn it ties ink to a deed's legal form, the signed sense the definition avoids (Q42), so colour at most, and never a hint that Laura notarise anything (Q55-044).
Mon 16 Nov: store only, colour; seam seals verified (Notary Act arts. 84, 105, re-read today); the two-ends mapping is forced and a second seal image breaks one turn per part.

Mon 16 Nov: sizes a Taiwan notary's fee against Laura's own bottom, which reads as advice to notarise her gift (Q55-044 dropped the deed; case A13); NT$3.1m for the bottom is Keel arithmetic not in NUMBERS (only NT$3.77m for the top, 8j).

Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3e colour; a family house gift, not a pledge to a nonprofit; fix the mapping: Laura's bottom is owned and held for her, never has already moved (it is paid in December 2032); read in a third-party copy.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e area (3), or beside the Taiwan-pledges reserve: a real Taiwanese capital pledge, approved by resolution, half paid and half withdrawn, a case of IPS l.15's co-sponsor falling short; re-read in LawPlayer's copy today, quote exact; say the withdrawal came after five years with no construction started, one court, appeal unknown; never call the paid half ink (Q50-008); never legal advice.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; a law firm's view against Keelung 2011 and the 2024 test, secondary and conflicting, so S 2.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; conflicting secondary sources (a law firm, a blog digest) and the High Court ruling unread; legal detail no part needs.

Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3d context: even the government's model founder pledge, sealed with the registered seal, promises to move money later, and the regulator then asks for bank proof (Q48-038 to Q48-041); never a form or step for Laura (case A13).
Mon 16 Nov: store only; founding paperwork for an arts foundation; that funders know a seal is identity, not money, is Keel's inference, not the source's.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, how Taiwanese capital pledges are written: a signed intent or consent form, no seal or notary, and a receipt only once cash or a registered transfer arrives (the counting clock of Q75-042); supports her figure stated in plain written form; forms read in part; never call paid money ink (Q50-008).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3.0 contrast: a Taiwanese capital gift goes from a letter of intent to money in a dedicated account, and a foundation's ten-year promise stays a promise, against Laura's ten owned (pairs with Q55-045); reword the idea cell's pencil to ink as letter to money, since ink stays owned in Treasuries (Q50-008); one university's own report.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; in public arts grants the grantee seals and the funder commits by decision and budget (Q43); one form read in a 2017 county copy.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 or 3d, one turn in the team's sentence; re-read at source today on Taipei's voucher sheet (擦刮挖補塗改、鉛筆書寫、墨跡不勻無效, exact); it governs grantees' spending receipts, so it shows why a pencil figure is not counted, never what co-sponsors count in a pledge (the card's best five overclaims); use at most one of rows 16 and 29.
Mon 16 Nov: store only, 3e context; Taipei's receipt clause re-read at source today (退回部份或全部補助款, exact); normal grant terms, not a co-sponsor falling short.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d guard and turn, re-read at source today, exact: faked works can bear genuine seals, so a seal proves who stamped, not what stands behind it; keeps the 3d seal honest without Taiwan law (row 2's point, in scope), and behind Laura's are Treasuries held for her; the team's sentence, never her words.
